title: Play whack-a-mole with the game's mallet: bop each mole the moment it lights, never one that is dark
instruction: Play one round of the whack-a-mole game with its mallet: pick the mallet up from the desk, then each time a mole lights up, bop that mole down with the mallet's head before its light goes out. Do not bop moles that are not lit, do not touch the moles with your fingers, and do not touch the game's switch or buttons: the round is started for you.
context: Whack-a-mole is the arcade game everyone knows, and its tabletop version is a common child's toy: a unit with five mole heads that light up one at a time at random, and a plastic mallet to bop them. This task is one round of that play, scored by the game's own rules: a lit mole bopped in time is a hit, a dark mole bopped costs points. The robot cannot learn the order or the timing beforehand, because both are drawn at random every episode. It must hold a mallet whose head is off to one side of its grip, watch the unit, see which mole has lit, put the head squarely on a small dome 75 mm from its neighbours, press it past the switch within about a second and a half, and lift clear for the next one, eight times in a row, without hitting the neighbours or the dark moles. On video: a red light jumps from mole to mole and the mallet comes down on each lit mole, which goes dark as it is hit.
setup: Metres; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the desk top; arm bases at (0, +0.305) and (0, -0.305). (1) Light-up tabletop whack-a-mole game unit (moulded plastic, battery powered), 267 x 267 mm, deck 70 mm high, 0.59 kg, on its rubber feet, square to the bench, centre at (0.21, -0.10). Five moles with yellow hard-hat domes (37 mm across) stand up out of the deck, tops 104.5 mm above the desk: one in the middle (0.21, -0.10) and four at (0.21 +/- 0.075, -0.10 +/- 0.075). Each sinks 9 mm when bopped, on a spring (1.2 N to start it moving, 2.3 N at the bottom); 4 mm of travel registers a press. Its controls (on/off switch, player and level buttons) sit on the deck's far edge between the far moles; before the trial the person running it switches it on and chooses one player and the easier level; the robot must not touch them. (2) One of the game's mallets (red plastic, 35 g): head 40 mm across and 65 mm long, handle 18 mm round, 145 mm overall, lying on the desk to the unit's right with the head's centre at (0.265, -0.31), the handle pointing back toward the robot. Layout, dome size, travel, forces and mallet size are estimates. Both arms at the ready pose, grippers open. Tape outlines mark the unit and the mallet. The round starts 1 s after the mallet is lifted 50 mm (the person running the trial presses start), or 30 s into the trial at the latest.
scoring: Score 0 if a mole was pressed with a gripper finger instead of the mallet, the robot (a finger or the mallet's head) touched the unit's on/off switch or buttons, the mallet fell off the desk, the game unit was shoved more than 30 mm or tipped more than 10 degrees, or no lit mole was hit. Otherwise the lower of two numbers. Hits (lit moles bopped down past their switch while lit by the head of the held mallet; a press by the handle, a loose mallet or the gripper puts the light out with no hit; the round lights 8): 8 = 1.0; 6-7 = 0.75; 4-5 = 0.5; 1-3 = 0.25. Wrong bops (a mole bopped while not lit): none = 1.0; 1-2 = 0.75; 3-4 = 0.5; 5 or more = 0. Doing nothing scores 0. Success: 1.0 (all 8, no wrong bop) held 1 s. In a real trial: count lit-mole hits (lights put out by the head of the mallet in the hand) and unlit bops on the trial video; the video shows any touch on the switch or buttons, and an end photo shows the unit still on, at the easier level, inside its tape outline.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz); the round itself lasts about 20-25 s
reset_notes: Switch the unit off and on, choose one player and the easier level. Put the unit back on its tape outline, square to the bench, and the mallet on its tape outline (head's centre at the mark, handle toward the robot). Ready pose, grippers open. A new round draws a new random order by itself. About 20 s a trial.
fidelity: The unit's electronics are a script: 8 lightings a round, a random mole (never the same twice running), lit 1.6 s or until hit, 0.6-1.4 s dark between; a hit needs the lit mole pushed 4 mm down by the held mallet's head (0.25 s debounce). Each point counts 1 (the middle mole's bonus is left out). The lit dome is shown as a red lamp. Moles are rigid sliders on preloaded springs; the mallet is rigid. Timings, layout, sizes, forces and masses are estimates.
